CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY PLAINS, AND WESTON COUNTY PLAINS...

.Warm temperatures, humidities as low as 13%, and southwest winds
gusting to 50 mph ahead of an approaching cold front will create
widespread critical fire weather conditions Friday afternoon through
Friday evening. Southwest winds increase over northeastern Wyoming
after 10 am Friday morning with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and
gusts of 40 to 50 mph through the afternoon. Winds will shift to the
northwest after midnight as the front moves through. While some
showers may accompany the front, not expecting any widespread wetting
rains.

Warning in effect from 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

* WHEN...Through late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 21 at 12:35PM CDT by NWS Jackson MS
properties.description:
According to local forestry agencies and the U.S. Forest Service,
recent longstanding drought conditions have led to extremely dry
fuels, making outdoor burning increasingly hazardous. Conditions
are such that a spark from equipment, the heat from a catalytic
converter, or any heat source could start a grass or brush fire.
The combination of dry fine fuels, such as grass, and low relative
humidity will continue to result elevated fire danger across the
region this week.

Minimum relative humidity values will range from upper teens to
below 30 percent during the daytime hours the next couple of days,
supporting increased fire danger given the longstanding drought
conditions and extremely dry and wildfire prone fuels. 20ft winds
remain light during this timeframe.

These extremely dry conditions will support the spread of
wildfires, even with light winds. Outdoor burning and activities
that involve open sparks or flames are discouraged and extra
caution is advised with any open burning. Please report all
wildfires to local law enforcement as soon as possible.

Numerous counties and parishes are under local burn bans at the
present time. Fires place local forestry agencies, fire departments,
and other fire control agencies in life threatening situations,
and can endanger communities. Please use caution and help prevent
forest and grass fires.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...All of northern and central Arizona.

* WHEN...Through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An upper-level trough will bring a deep surge of subtropical and
tropical moisture into our region. Showers and thunderstorms will
develop across much of northern and central Arizona early
Wednesday morning and continue through Thursday evening. Stronger
thunderstorms will bring threats of Flash Flooding, while more
prolonged rainfall could lead to elevated flow in streams,
rivers, and washes.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves due to
elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet expected.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles
County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor beach erosion and tidal overflows may
occur across south-facing beaches especially along the Malibu
Coast and in the Long Beach area.
properties.instruction:

stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.
